questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgement?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgement.
It harms both driving skills and judgement.
It does not affect driving skills or judgement.
It harms driving skills but not judgement.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgement.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also impairs your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis happens when you:

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Take frequent rest stops.
Get too much sleep before driving.
Take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stare straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare at the road and stop looking around your vehicle. You may zone out and not notice traffic slowing or stopping ahead of you.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.
Road curve.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming ahead.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make any driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Sits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Stops the seat belt warning light or buzzer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signal before you change lanes or exit a freeway. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move left or right.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, moving into a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when a stop sign is present, or when flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires with poor tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and look at your blind spots before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Always obey them.
They are only suggestions.
Follow them only when other cars are around.
Follow them only when a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and help guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines are doubled in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the overhead clearance is low.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Only drive on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the single best thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel is a distraction and can cause a crash.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
You can drive through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back-seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, develop a habit of buckling your own seat belt and making sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is coming. Drive carefully in areas where pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road carefully and park as far off as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane. Be ready to merge smoothly.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. A train or other vehicle may be on the tracks.

questions.question: You are involved in an accident. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a Yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles go first. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop. The driver who arrives first at the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are driving on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guardrail.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth and correct air pressure. Slow down in the rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor safety problem.
A serious safety problem.
Safe if you have only a few drinks.
Dangerous only to the driver.

questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It endangers you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Divided highway ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown, which is 35 mph.

questions.question: A passenger in a moving car cannot:

options.text: Use a cell phone.
Sleep.
Have an open container of alcohol.
Use a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an open container of alcohol.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink from or hold an open alcohol container in a moving car on a public road. The driver can be punished for this violation.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic may be coming toward you from the opposite direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that an island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Cannot pass another vehicle.
May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass only at night.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white and rectangular with black markings. Drivers must follow all instructions on these signs. Where this sign is posted, passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds before. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. If there are multiple lanes, move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Only turn when it is safe.

questions.question: On long trips, you can stay awake by:

options.text: Turning on the radio.
Driving slower.
Stopping regularly to rest.
Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks. Stop to rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells drivers to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You may proceed when it is safe.
